questions.prompt: A user authenticates successfully to an Azure SMB file share and has Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor. A directory ACL denies the user access. What is the expected result?

options.text: Access to that directory is denied.
options.explanation: Share access does not override the directory's Windows ACL.

options.text: The Contributor assignment overrides every directory ACL.
Azure automatically retries with the storage account key.
options.explanation: Identity access does not silently become an administrative key mount.
Neither share RBAC nor an ACL enables anonymous SMB access.

questions.prompt: A group needs to read files through identity-based Azure Files SMB. Its directory ACLs already allow read. Which share-level role supplies the required read access?

options.text: Storage File Data SMB Share Reader.
options.explanation: This role grants the SMB share-level read permission.
Blob roles do not authorize Azure Files SMB reads.
ARM resource visibility is not SMB data access.
Blob delegation-key generation is unrelated to SMB share access.

questions.prompt: A storage account uses AD DS for identity-based Azure Files SMB authentication. Can one share in that same account independently use Entra Domain Services as a second simultaneous identity source?

options.text: No; one identity source is configured per storage account.
options.explanation: Separate identity-source requirements require a different account design.

options.text: Yes; every share independently selects its identity source.
options.explanation: The source is configured at the account level.

options.text: Yes; adding an ACL switches the authentication provider.
Yes; a stored access policy selects the provider.
options.explanation: SAS policies do not select SMB Kerberos identity sources.
